rationale: GATE A OF THE BARE-READ RULE (a name is not a read unless it resolves to a declared member of the enclosing type AND is not a declaration's own name). Two declaration positions were MISSING from that gate's parent-type list, and probe on the pinned grammar showed both fabricating a read: a COMPACT CONSTRUCTOR's own name `R { ... }` (JLS 8.10.4) emitted `uses R -> R`, and an ANNOTATION TYPE ELEMENT's declaration `List<String> list();` (JLS 9.6.1) emitted `uses Ann -> list`. Both are names being DECLARED, not members being read, and GATE A let them through because the member map carried the same name. Authored from Java semantics before the fix. The positive row pins that the fix did not silence legitimate reads: the compact constructor body's `x` (the record component read on line 6) must still emit. The forbids are the two fabrications, one per fixed position.

forbidRelationships.comment: a compact constructor's own name is its identity, not a read
an annotation type element DECLARES `list`; the declaration's name is not a read of it
same rule for the second element declaration
the annotation type's own name is never a read
